lines: Blessed be He who spoke so that the world came into
being, blessed be He who speaks and acts, blessed be He
who decrees and fulfils, blessed be He who has mercy on the
earth, blessed be He who has mercy on the creatures, blessed
be He who grants those that fear Him a good reward, blessed
be He who lives forever and exists for eternity, blessed be
the Redeemer and Deliverer, blessed be His Name. Blessed
art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, God the
merciful father who is praised by the mouth of His people,
extolled and glorified by the tongue of His devoted ones and
His servants. Through the songs of David Thy servant will
we praise Thee, O Lord our God, with songs of praise and
hymns will we magnify Thee, praise Thee and glorify Thee
and recall Thy Name and crown Thee as our King, our God,
unique and everlasting, the King whose great Name is extolled
and glorified for ever. Blessed art Thou, O Lord King cel-
ebrated in paeons of praise.

Blessed art Thou, O Lord King celebrated in paeons of praise.

lines: Thank the Lord, invoke His Name, proclaim His deeds
among the peoples. Sing to Him, play music to Him, tell of
all His wonders. Take pride in His holy Name; let the heart
of those who seek the Lord, rejoice. Search for the Lord and
His strength, seek His countenance constantly. Remember
His wonders which He has performed, His signs and the
judgments of His mouth. O seed of His servant Israel, sons
of Jacob His elect, He is the Lord our God, over the whole
earth are His judgments. Remember for ever His convenant,
the word which He has commanded for thousands of genera-
tions, which He contracted with Abraham and swore to Isaac.

lines: He established it as Law for Jacob, for Israel as an eternal
convenant, saying: To you will I give the land of Canaan
as the portion of your inheritance, though you are small in
number, few and strangers in it. They wandered from nation
to nation, from one kingdom to another people. He let no
man oppress them and rebuked kings because of them. Do not
touch my anointed ones, to my prophets do no harm. Sing
to the Lord, all the earth, proclaim from day to day His
salvation. Tell of His glory among the nations and among all
peoples of His wonders. For great is the Lord and most
renowned, and more awe-inspiring than all deities. For all
the deities of the peoples are idols — the Lord has made the
heavens. Splendour and beauty are before Him, might and
glory are in His place. Ascribe to the Lord, O families of the
peoples, ascribe to the Lord honour and might. Ascribe to
the Lord the glory of His Name, bring a gift and come before
Him, bow before the Lord in sacred adornment. Tremble
before Him, all the earth, though the world be firm and does
not totter. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth revel and
among the nations let them say: The Lord reigns. Let the sea
roar and the fullness of it, let the field and all that is in it be
joyful. Then will trees of the forest exult before the Lord
when He comes to judge the earth. Thank the Lord for He
is good, for His grace endures for ever. And say: Save us,
God of our salvation, and gather us and deliver us from the
nations, so that we may thank Thy holy Name and extol Thy
fame. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from eternity
to eternity. And the whole people said Amen and praised the
Lord. Extol the Lord our God and bow before His footstool,
for He is holy. Extol the Lord our God and bow before His
holy mountain, for holy is the Lord our God. He is compas-
sionate, grants atonement for guilt and does not destroy;
many a time does He avert His anger nor does He arouse the
whole of His wrath. Thou, O Lord, dost not withhold Thy
compassion from me, Thy grace and Thy truth always protect
me. Remember Thy compassion, O Lord, and Thine acts of
kindness for they are from eternity. Ascribe might to God,

lines: over Israel is His supremacy and His might is in the skies.
Awe-inspiring art Thou, O God, from Thy sanctuary the God
of Israel. He gives might and strength to the people, blessed
be God. God of vengeance is the Lord, O God of vengeance,
appear. Arise, O Judge of the earth, render retribution to the
proud. Salvation is the Lord’s, may Thy blessing come upon
Thy people (Selah). The Lord of Hosts is with us, a refuge
for us is the God of Jacob (Selah). Lord of Hosts, fortunate
the man who trusts in Thee. O Lord, save; may the King
answer us on the day we call. Save Thy people and bless Thine
inheritance, pasture them and bear them for ever. Our soul
waits for the Lord, He is our help and our shield. For in Him
will our heart rejoice, for in His holy Name do we trust. Let
Thy grace, O Lord, be upon us just as we wait for Thee.
Show us, O Lord, Thy grace, and give us Thy salvation. Arise
to be our help and redeem us for the sake of Thy grace. I am
the Lord your God, who has brought you up from the land of
Egypt, open your mouth wide and I will fill it. Fortunate the
people to whom the like of this happens, fortunate the people
whose God is the Lord. And I trust in Thy grace, my heart
revels in Thy salvation, I sing to the Lord for He has treated
me well.

lines: For the conductor of the Choir, a Psalm by
David: The heavens tell of the glory of God, and the firma-
ment proclaims the work of His hand. Day utters speech to
day and night to night expresses knowledge. There is neither
speech nor words without their sound being heard. Their line
goes out over the whole earth and at the ends of the world
are their words, for the sun has He set a tent among them.
And he (the sun) comes forth like a bridegroom from his
canopy, rejoices like a hero to run a course. At one end of
the heavens is his starting point and his circuit goes round to
the other end — nothing can hide from his glow. The Torah
of the Lord is flawless, refreshing the soul, the testimony of
the Lord is faithful making the simple wise. The precepts of
the Lord are upright, causing the heart to rejoice, the com-
mandment of the Lord is clear, giving light to the eyes. The
fear of the Lord is pure, enduring for ever, the judgments of

gold, even than an abundance of refined gold, and sweeter
than honey and the honeycomb. Your servant, too, is careful
about them, for keeping them there is great reward. As for
errors, who understands, cleanse me from hidden sins. From
the arrogant, too, keep away Thy servant — let them not
rule over me; then will I be without fault and clear of grave
offence. May the words of my mouth be pleasing and the
meditation of my heart before Thee, O Lord my Rock and
my Redeemer.

lines: By David when he disguised his sanity before
Abimelech, who drove him away and he went: I will at all
times bless the Lord, His fame shall always be in my mouth.
My soul glories in the Lord, let the humble hear and rejoice.
Magnify the Lord with me and let us exalt His Name together.
I sought the Lord, and He answered me and saved me from
all my terrors. When they look to Him, they are radiant and
their faces are not shamed. This man called and the Lord
hears and from all his troubles did He save him. An angel of
the Lord encamps around those that fear Him and rescued
them: Observe and perceive that the Lord is good, fortunate
the man who trusts in Him. Fear the Lord, O His holy ones,
for there is no want among those that fear Him. Though
whelps may hunger and starve, those that seek the Lord will
not lack all that is good. Come, children, listen to me, the
fear of the Lord will I teach you. Who is the man that desires
life, who longs for days to see goodness? Keep your tongue
from evil and your lips from speaking guile, depart from
evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it. The eyes of the
Lord are towards the righteous and His ears to their cry.
The countenance of the Lord is against evil-doers to cut off
their memory from the earth. Men cry out and the Lord

lines: The Prayer of Moses the man of God: Lord,
Thou hast been a dwelling for us in every generation. Before
the mountains were born and Thou didst bring forth the
earth and the world, from eternity to eternity Thou art God.
Thou dost restore mortals to contrition and say: Return,
children of men. For a thousand years are in Thine eyes as a
yesterday that passes and as a watch in the night. Thou hast
carried them off: they are in sleep; in the morning he is
renewed like grass. In the morning it blossoms and is re-
newed, in the evening it withers and dries. For we are
consumed through Thine anger and terrified through Thy
wrath. Thou hast placed our sins before Thee, our secret
transgressions before the light of Thy countenance. For all
our days pass away through Thine anger, we end our years
like a fleeting thought. The days of our years — they are
seventy years or, at full strength, eighty years, and their pride
is toil and sorrow, since swiftly severed do we fly away. Who
knows the might of Thine anger and is Thy wrath according to
the fear of Thee? To count our days teach us well so that we
may acquire a wise heart. Turn again, O Lord — how much
longer — and take pity on Thy servants. Satisfy us in the
morning with Thy grace that we may exult and rejoice all our
days. Cause us to rejoice as long as the days when Thou didst
afflict us and the years when we saw misfortune. Let Thy
work become apparent to Thy servants, and Thy splendour
to their children; and may the favour of the Lord our God
be upon us; and firmly establish the work of our hands for
us, the work of our hands, establish it firmly.

lines: the Lord: My refuge and my fortress, my God in whom I
trust. For He saves you from the snare of the fowler, from
destructive plague. With His wing He covers you, you shelter
under His wings, His faithfulness is shield and buckler. You
shall not fear the terror of night, the arrow that flies by day,
the plague that creeps in the dark, the pestilence that flares
up at noon. Though a thousand fall at your side and ten
thousand on your right, to you it will not approach. You
need only look with your eyes and you will see the recompense
of the wicked. For Thou, O Lord, art my trust — on high hast
Thou placed Thy dwelling. No misfortune will befall you, no
plague will come near your tent. For He will command His
angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways. On
hands will they bear you lest your foot be bruised by a stone.
Though you tread on the lion and viper and trample on the
whelp and the crocodile. For because he delighted in Me I
delivered him; I shall raise him up because he acknowledged
my Name. When he calls me, I will answer him, I am with
him in distress, I save him and honour him. With length of
days will I satisfy him and I will let him see my salvation.

lines: Exult, O righteous ones, in the Lord, it is
becoming to the upright to give praise. Thank the Lord with
the zither, with the ten-stringed harp make music to Him.
Sing to Him a new song, pluck the strings well in triumph.
For upright is the word of the Lord and all His work is with
faithfulness. He loves righteousness and justice, the grace of
the Lord fills the earth. Through the word of the Lord were
the heavens made and through the breath of His mouth all
their host. He gathers like a heap the waters of the seas, and
puts the depths into store-chambers. The whole earth is afraid
before the Lord, before Him do all inhabitants of the world
tremble. For He spoke and it was, He commanded and there
it stood. The Lord has frustrated the plan of nations, baffled
the thoughts of peoples. The counsel of the Lord endures for
ever, the thoughts of His heart from generation to generation.
Fortunate the nation whose God is the Lord, the people which
He has chosen as His inheritance. The Lord has looked from
heaven, He has seen all the sons of man. From His dwelling
place does He watch over all the inhabitants of the earth.
He who has formed their hearts altogether, He understands
all their deeds. The king is not saved by the size of an army,
the warrior will not escape through the measure of strength.
Useless is the horse for victory, by the measure of its might

lines: (Psalm 92.)
blocks.text: (Psalm 92.)

lines: A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: It is good
to thank the Lord and to sing praise to Thy Name, O Most
High, to proclaim Thy kindness in the morning and Thy
faithfulness at night, on the ten-stringed harp, through med-
itation on the zither. For Thou hast gladdened me, O Lord,
with Thy deeds, in the works of Thy hands do I exult. How
great are Thy works, O Lord, profound indeed are Thy
thoughts. A simpleton cannot know, nor can a fool under-
stand this, when the wicked flourish like grass and all evil-
doers blossom forth only to be destroyed for ever. But Thou
art supreme to eternity, O Lord. Behold Thine enemies, O
Lord, behold Thine enemies shall perish, all evil-doers shall
scatter. Then shalt Thou lift up my horn like the unicorn,
I am anointed with fresh oil. Then shall my eye look down
upon my adversaries, when evil men rise up against me my
ears shall hear. The righteous shall flourish like the palm,
like the cedar on Lebanon shall he grow. Those planted in
the House of the Lord shall blossom forth in the courts of
our God. They will yet be luxuriant in old age, full of sap
and fresh will they be, so as to proclaim that the Lord is
upright, my Rock in whom there is no wrong.

lines: (Psalm 93.)
blocks.text: (Psalm 93.)

lines: The Lord reigns, clothed in majesty, the Lord
clothes Himself in strength, He girds Himself. Surely the
world stands firm without shaking. Thy throne is established
from of old, since eternity art Thou. The streams, O Lord,
the streams have raised their voice, the streams shall raise
their roar. Mightier than many waters are the breakers of the
sea but still mightier on high is the Lord. Thy testimonies
are indeed sure, holiness becomes Thine House, O Lord, for
an infinity of days.
